insights.insight: At 9,290 verified receipts and $689K in confirmed GMV, every signal in this network is a cryptographic proof of purchase — not an inference. The ad industry pays $5+ CPM for probabilistic targeting built on behavioral guesses; this protocol produces the thing those guesses are trying to approximate.

The 7-day GMV window has gone from $53K on April 1 to a peak of $111.8K on April 7 — more than doubling in eight days. A structural floor near $100K/week is forming, with recovery to that level now happening within four hours of each midnight rollback.

insights.topic: Retail and grocery as anchor categories
insights.insight: Retail/department stores leads all categories at ~$154 per receipt, while grocery leads in receipt volume at 582 transactions — together they account for the highest-frequency, highest-value purchase signals in the network. For CPG and mass-market retail brands, these are the categories where verified commerce data is densest.

insights.topic: Amazon and Depop confirm e-commerce and resale are structural
insights.insight: Amazon at 76 receipts in the trailing 14 days is not incidental — it ranks second among all brands and confirms digital purchase verification is working at scale alongside physical retail. Depop's sustained top-five presence signals that secondary market and resale commerce has entered the verified data set, a segment most brand measurement systems ignore entirely.

insights.topic: Receipt correction event — ledger integrity to monitor
insights.insight: Between April 8 04:15 and 07:56, cumulative GMV dropped from $684,959 to $668,833 and receipt count fell simultaneously — the first observed reversal in any cycle. Rolling windows were unaffected and cumulative GMV has since recovered to a new high, pointing to a restatement rather than a throughput problem, but this is a data quality signal worth tracking for recurrence.

insights.topic: DKIM vendor mix reveals digital-native commerce layer
insights.insight: Verified senders include Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, Amazon, OpenAI, and Suno — a cross-section of SaaS, creator economy, and AI-product transactions sitting alongside physical retail receipts. For brands trying to reach digitally-active, high-intent buyers, this network is already capturing purchase behavior that conventional retail panels miss.
